original_query: select  i_item_desc       ,w_warehouse_name       ,d1.d_week_seq       ,sum(case when p_promo_sk is null then 1 else 0 end) no_promo       ,sum(case when p_promo_sk is not null then 1 else 0 end) promo       ,count(*) total_cnt from catalog_sales join inventory on (cs_item_sk = inv_item_sk) join warehouse on (w_warehouse_sk=inv_warehouse_sk) join item on (i_item_sk = cs_item_sk) join customer_demographics on (cs_bill_cdemo_sk = cd_demo_sk) join household_demographics on (cs_bill_hdemo_sk = hd_demo_sk) join date_dim d1 on (cs_sold_date_sk = d1.d_date_sk) join date_dim d2 on (inv_date_sk = d2.d_date_sk) join date_dim d3 on (cs_ship_date_sk = d3.d_date_sk) left outer join promotion on (cs_promo_sk=p_promo_sk) left outer join catalog_returns on (cr_item_sk = cs_item_sk and cr_order_number = cs_order_number) where d1.d_week_seq = d2.d_week_seq   and inv_quantity_on_hand < cs_quantity   and d3.d_date > d1.d_date + interval '3 day'   and hd_buy_potential = '1001-5000'   and d1.d_year = 2001   and cd_marital_status = 'U'   and cd_dep_count between 5 and 7   and i_category IN ('Books', 'Home', 'Sports')   and cs_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 80 AND 100 group by i_item_desc,w_warehouse_name,d1.d_week_seq order by total_cnt desc, i_item_desc, w_warehouse_name, d_week_seq limit 100;
rewritten_query:
SELECT
    i.i_item_desc,
    w.w_warehouse_name,
    d1.d_week_seq,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE cs.cs_promo_sk IS NULL) AS no_promo,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE cs.cs_promo_sk IS NOT NULL) AS promo,
    COUNT(*) AS total_cnt
FROM catalog_sales cs
JOIN date_dim d1
  ON cs.cs_sold_date_sk = d1.d_date_sk
 AND d1.d_year = 2001
JOIN inventory inv
  ON cs.cs_item_sk = inv.inv_item_sk
JOIN date_dim d2
  ON inv.inv_date_sk = d2.d_date_sk
 AND d2.d_week_seq = d1.d_week_seq
JOIN warehouse w
  ON w.w_warehouse_sk = inv.inv_warehouse_sk
JOIN item i
  ON i.i_item_sk = cs.cs_item_sk
 AND i.i_category IN ('Books', 'Home', 'Sports')
JOIN customer_demographics cd
  ON cs.cs_bill_cdemo_sk = cd.cd_demo_sk
 AND cd.cd_marital_status = 'U'
 AND cd.cd_dep_count BETWEEN 5 AND 7
JOIN household_demographics hd
  ON cs.cs_bill_hdemo_sk = hd.hd_demo_sk
 AND hd.hd_buy_potential = '1001-5000'
JOIN date_dim d3
  ON cs.cs_ship_date_sk = d3.d_date_sk
 AND d3.d_date > d1.d_date + INTERVAL '3 day'
WHERE cs.cs_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 80 AND 100
  AND inv.inv_quantity_on_hand < cs.cs_quantity
GROUP BY i.i_item_desc, w.w_warehouse_name, d1.d_week_seq
ORDER BY total_cnt DESC, i.i_item_desc, w.w_warehouse_name, d1.d_week_seq
LIMIT 100;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Removed the unused LEFT JOIN to catalog_returns. It contributes no columns to SELECT/WHERE/GROUP BY; the provided plan already eliminates it (unique on cr_item_sk, cr_order_number), so it is safe to drop from the query text.

Removed the LEFT JOIN to promotion. Under TPC-DS referential integrity, cs_promo_sk is either NULL or a valid p_promo_sk, so p_promo_sk IS NULL is equivalent to cs_promo_sk IS NULL. This eliminates one join and promotion scan.
Replaced SUM(CASE ...) aggregates with COUNT(*) FILTER (...), which is clearer and produces the same plan or slightly better.

Moved table-local predicates (d_year, i_category, cd_* filters, hd_buy_potential, d3 date comparison) into the corresponding JOIN ON clauses for readability; for inner joins this is semantically identical and does not hinder the optimizer.
No CTEs were introduced: there are no redundant subquery computations, and the many existing JOIN/WHERE conditions would make CTE decomposition add overhead without benefit.
